description: A man seen from behind, in a crimson velvet robe with fur trim, gold-embroidered sleeves and a jewelled belt with a sword at his hip, raises a folded paper in one hand. He faces a crowd of bearded men in fur hats, caps and robes, some with raised hands, in a vaulted stone hall lit by candles, a torch and a window; one man on the right wears plate armour. The painting fills the frame edge to edge. No letters or numbers are visible, and nothing is violent or bloody.
reason: The picture is a generic 16th-century court or assembly scene: a nobleman raises a document before a crowd. Nothing marks it as the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth or its religious tolerance, so it could illustrate any European court. A reviewer should decide whether this stands for the Golden Age.
